content.text:
The construction loop is running as a background workflow (`/workflows` to watch it live). Its shape:

- **Analyse** — one agent per pass re-runs `openspec instructions apply --change bolt-abc --json` fresh and infers the dependency graph from the task prose alone, returning startable ids (with reasons) and waiting ids (with what they block on).
- **Build** — one agent per startable task, in parallel, each writing only its own `out/<id>.txt`.
- **Checkoff** — a single serialized agent flips the `- [ ]` boxes in `tasks.md`, so the shared file is never edited concurrently; the next pass then reads the updated state.

The loop repeats until nothing remains, and bails out early on a deadlock (remaining tasks but none startable) or a no-progress pass, capped at 6 passes.

Expected trajectory: pass 1 builds tasks 1 and 2 (task 3's description says it can't start until gateway-auth exists), pass 2 builds task 3, pass 3 sees zero remaining and exits. I'll report the actual result when it finishes.

The dependency was inferred from prose, as the schema requires: pass 1 held back task 3 because its description says it calls the gateway-auth endpoint and can't start until gateway-auth is built; pass 2 re-queried, saw task 1 now `done`, and released it. ### Design note

Builders ran in parallel but each wrote only its own `out/<id>.txt`; `tasks.md` is shared, so checkbox flips were done by a single serialized agent after each pass. That's what makes the next pass's re-query trustworthy — concurrent edits to one checklist file would have been the obvious failure mode here.

The loop also has two bail-outs it never needed: a deadlock exit (remaining tasks but none startable) and a no-progress exit, plus a 6-pass cap.

The construction loop is running as a background workflow (`/workflows` to watch it live). Its shape:

- **Analyse** — one agent per pass re-runs `openspec instructions apply --change bolt-abc --json` fresh and infers the dependency graph from the task prose alone, returning startable ids (with reasons) and waiting ids (with what they block on).

- **Checkoff** — a single serialized agent flips the `- [ ]` boxes in `tasks.md`, so the shared file is never edited concurrently; the next pass then reads the updated state.

The loop repeats until nothing remains, and bails out early on a deadlock (remaining tasks but none startable) or a no-progress pass, capped at 6 passes.
